cards.headline: E-7 Salary, Duties or Worksite Changed?
body: The employer may be the same, but immigration checks still matter.
cards.takeaway: Compare the proposed terms with the employee's existing E-7 approval before making changes.
cards.design: A large office building and three routes for salary, actual job duties and workplace changes.

cards.headline: Planning a Change—or Already Made One?

body.text: Compare the current E-7 approval with the proposed terms. If prior permission is required, obtain it before the change takes effect.
Check the actual date, pay, duties and worksite. Then establish which approval or reporting duties applied and whether any were missed.

cards.takeaway: Before a change, check the procedure; afterward, establish the actual facts and dates.
cards.design: Two contrasting calendars: a planned reassignment and a completed employment change.

cards.headline: Three Changes, Three Different Legal Checks

body.text: Compare the actual new pay terms with the wage criteria for that E-7 occupation.
Compare the main duties, not merely a new department name, with the approved occupation.
Distinguish office relocation from a branch move and check which procedure applies.

cards.takeaway: Even if one contract covers all three changes, assess each separately.
cards.design: Three routes using a payslip, briefcase and office building, each with a distinct checkpoint.

cards.headline: E-7-1 Pay Cut: Compare the Annual Figures
cards.takeaway: Separate rules may apply by occupation. A shortfall does not automatically revoke E-7 status.
cards.design: Three annual KRW bars in the same units, with the proposed pay below the general E-7-1 threshold.

cards.headline: Does a Salary Change Trigger a 15-Day Report?

body.text: A pay change alone is not separately listed as an employer-reporting event under Article 24(3) of the Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Control Act.
If a contract period or another legally listed item changes, check the employer's 15-day reporting duty and the statutory exceptions.

cards.takeaway: Identify the actual event and its exceptions; a salary amendment alone is not the test.
cards.design: Side-by-side documents: one amends pay only; another also changes a reportable term.

cards.headline: Same employer. Different terms. Separate checks.
cards.design: An uncluttered single-line visual pause, with a hand-drawn ring around 'Separate checks'.

cards.headline: New Department—or Different Actual Duties?

body.text: If Overseas Sales becomes International Business but actual duties stay the same, the name change alone does not require a new immigration status.
If overseas account management shifts mainly to domestic sales, check the new activities against the employee's approved E-7 occupation.

cards.takeaway: Assess the duties the employee actually performs, not just the job title.
cards.design: Left: new department name, same work. Right: an actual shift from overseas sales to domestic sales.

cards.headline: Worksite Changes: Three Different Situations

body.text: For an employer-wide relocation, review address-change reporting rules and exceptions.
Even within one company, compare the new branch with the approved worksite.
For ongoing on-site work, check the real work location and who directs the employee.

cards.takeaway: Workplace changes generally need prior permission; qualifying workers report within 15 days.
cards.design: Use different buildings and arrows to distinguish whole-office relocation, branch move and client placement.

cards.headline: Documents to Gather Before Reassignment
body: Records of the E-7 category, approved job duties and permitted workplace.
Existing contract showing salary, contract term and work location.
Proposed pay terms, job description, reassignment notice and effective date.
If already changed, actual payroll, duties, worksite and change dates.
cards.takeaway: Compare the existing E-7 approval with the proposed or actual working conditions.
cards.design: A four-part document checklist designed for employers to save before changes take effect.

cards.headline: What Should Your Company Check First?

body.text: Gather current E-7 approval details, the existing employment contract, and proposed pay, duties, worksite and effective date.
Identify wage and activity rules, which immigration procedures need checking, and missing documents. Detailed written reviews and filings are separate.

cards.takeaway: A free initial check can identify which immigration steps and documents to verify first.
cards.design: Two readable panels: what HR prepares and what an initial review identifies; a single CTA at the bottom.
